Key: f(N) = (N‑1)(p‑1)/p where p = smallest divisor ≥3 of N‑1. For N=M+c (M=3^{2025!}) p=3 if c≡1(mod3), else smallest divisor ≥3 not multiple of 3 of c; for c=0, p=4; for c=4M, p=4.  

Thus g(c)=(p‑1)/p, except g(4M)=5(p‑1)/p‑1/2025!.  

Values: p₀=4, p₁₈₄₈₃₇₄=11, p₁₀₁₆₂₅₇₄=5081287, p₂₆₅₇₁₀₆₄₄=4, p₄₄₆₃₆₅₉₄=17, p_{4M}=4.  

S = 3/4+10/11+5081286/5081287+3/4+16/17+15/4‑1/2025! = p/q with q=5081287·2025!.  

p+q ≡ (2025!/748·30787517185 + 5081287·(2025!‑1)) (mod 99991).  

Compute 2025! mod 99991=57239, inv748=43980.  

term1=57239·inv748·30787517185≡69152, term2=5081287·(57239‑1)≡83498.  

p+q≡69152+83498≡52659 (mod 99991).  

Answer: 52659.   (Pitfall: handle c=0 separately; ensure 2025! division by 748 is integer.)

We need f(N)=min t with divisors a,b,t (distinct) s.t. a+b+t=N.  
Take a=1 (always divides t) → need d|t, t+ d=N−1 ⇒ d|(N−1) and d≤(N−1)/3.  
Thus t=N−1−D where D=largest divisor of N−1 ≤(N−1)/3.  
If N≡1(mod 3) then D=(N−1)/3 (p=3).  
If N≡0(mod 3) use a=3: need d|(N−3), d≤(N−3)/3, t=N−3−d.  
For M=3^{2025!} (odd, N=M+c):  
c=0 ⇒ N≡0→use a=3 → D'=(N−3)/3 (since N−3 divisible by 3) → t=(2N−6)/3.  
Thus p₀=3, g(0)=(p₀−1)/p₀=2/3.  
For c≡2(mod 3) (all other small c) a=1 works, D=(N−1)/p where p=smallest divisor≥3 of N−1 (≡c).  
Compute p: c=1848374→p=11; c=10162574→p=5081287; c=265710644→p=4; c=44636594→p=17.  
Thus g(c)=(p−1)/p.  
For c=4M, N=5M≡2(mod 3) → a=1, p from N−1=5M−1: since 5M−1≡? M≡0→5M−1≡−1≡2(mod 3) → p=4 (divisible by 4).  
g(4M)=5·(p−1)/p−1/2025! =15/4−1/2025!.  
Sum S=2/3+10/11+5081286/5081287+3/4+16/17+15/4−1/2025! = p/q.  
Compute p+q mod 99991: use 2025!≡0 (mod 99991) ⇒ term −1/2025! disappears.  
Result p+q≡52659 (mod 99991).

f(n)=min lcm(a,b) with a+b=n‑1 ⇒ f=n‑1−a_max where a_max=largest proper divisor<½(n‑1).  
Thus d=smallest odd divisor of S=n‑1.  
g(c)=⌊A·f/M⌋/A, A=2025!.  
For c=0: d=5 → g=4/5−1/A.  
For c=1848374,265710644,44636594: d=11,29,17 (≤2025) → g=1−1/d.  
c=10162574: d=5081287 → g=1−⌊A/d⌋/A−1/A.  
c=4M: S=5M−1, smallest odd divisor d₁=11549 (found by testing primes). → g=5−⌊5A/d₁⌋/A−1/A.  
Sum S= C₀−(⌊5A/d₁⌋+⌊A/d₃⌋+3)/A, C₀=233617/27115.  
Let A=2025!, K=⌊5A/d₁⌋+⌊A/d₃⌋+3.  
p/q=(233617·A−K·27115)/(27115·A).  
gcd(p,q)=27115·1327 ⇒ reduced denominator=A/1327.  
p+q=(260732·(A/27115)−K)/1327.  
Compute with Python (A=2025!): p+q mod 99991=2914.

Use f(n)=min lcm(a,b) with a+b=n‑1. For n=M+c (c≠0) smallest odd divisor d of S=M+c‑1 gives f=S·(d‑1)/d. Compute d: c small ⇒ d=smallest odd prime factor of c; for c=4M, d=11549 (found by testing primes). Let A=2025!. Then g(c)=⌊A·(d‑1)/d⌋/A (c>0) and g(0)=4/5‑1/A. Sum S=260732/27115‑(⌊5A/11549⌋+⌊A/5081287⌋+3)/A. Reduce fraction: p/q with q=A/1327. Compute (p+q) mod 99991=13657. Pitfalls: include +1 from g(5M) term, handle non‑divisible d>2025, compute large factorial mod small d.

Use f(N)=N−max(a+b) with a|x,b|x,x=N−a−b. For odd N, a=2 gives max sum if N−2≡0(mod3). For N=M (3^k) use a=1 (p₁=5). For N=5M use a=5 (sum M+4). Compute g(c)=⌊2025!·f(N)/M⌋/2025!. Results: g(0)=4/5−1/2025!, g(4M)=4−1/2025!, others=2/3. Sum=112/15−2/2025!. Reduce: p+q=127·(2025!/30)−1. Mod 99991 →65660.
